content: The study by Tierney et al. (2018) compared the use of tenofovir versus placebo in preventing perinatal transmission of hepatitis B, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Global guidelines have been established to validate the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B virus, with resources accessible through the World Health Organization (WHO). Marasciulo et al. conducted a systematic review on hepatocellular carcinoma during pregnancy, highlighting its clinical implications. Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) are antiviral agents used in managing hepatitis B, with detailed prescribing information available through regulatory agencies. The global prevalence, treatment, and prevention of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection were modeled in a 2018 study by Razavi-Shearer et al., emphasizing the burden of disease. Indolfi et al. (2019) reviewed HBV infection in children and adolescents, while Fofana et al. (2023) analyzed HBV in West African children, identifying factors such as HIV co-infection. Platt et al. (2020) conducted a meta-analysis on HBV co-infection among individuals living with HIV, revealing significant global prevalence. Schweitzer et al. (2015) estimated the worldwide prevalence of chronic HBV infection, while Ott et al. (2012) provided age-specific seroprevalence data. Sarin et al. (2016) updated the Asian-Pacific clinical practice guidelines for HBV management, and Liu et al. (2001) explored the genetic diversity of HBV in Belgian children. Belhassen-García et al. (2018) examined transmissible diseases, including HBV, in minors migrating to Spain. Gupta et al. (2008) investigated horizontal transmission of HBV among household contacts in North India. Unsafe injection practices as a risk factor for bloodborne viruses were highlighted by Gupta et al. (2013). Jonas et al. (2016) and Murray et al. (2012) conducted randomized trials on antiviral therapies, such as entecavir and tenofovir, in children and adolescents with chronic HBV. Waalewijn et al. (2023) provided pharmacokinetic data on TAF in African children, while Schwarz et al. (2022) evaluated the safety and efficacy of TAF in pediatric patients. Zhang et al. (2021) developed non-invasive models to predict liver fibrosis in children with chronic HBV. Pavlovic et al. (2016) and Xu et al. (2021) assessed liver fibrosis using transient elastography in pediatric populations. Rodriguez-Baez et al. (2020) described hepatic histology in treatment-naïve children with chronic HBV in North America. Yang et al. (2015) reported that hepatocellular carcinoma occurs at an earlier age in Africans with chronic HBV. Mason et al. (2016) studied HBV DNA integration in immune-tolerant patients. Fung et al. (2017) compared TDF with emtricitabine/TDF in lamivudine-resistant HBV over five years. Surial et al. (2021) examined metabolic changes after switching from TDF to TAF in individuals with HIV. Ling et al. (2021) highlighted the under-treatment of chronic HBV in children in North America. Lok et al. (2007) standardized nomenclature for antiviral drug-resistant HBV, while Locarnini (2008) discussed resistance pathways. Fung et al. (2006) and Yim et al. (2006) explored virologic responses to adefovir and the evolution of multidrug-resistant HBV. Pallier et al. (2006) analyzed lamivudine resistance dynamics, and Leung (2008) reviewed nucleos(t)ide analogues for chronic HBV. Yeh et al. (2000) described the emergence of distinct lamivudine-resistant mutants. Mokaya et al. (2020) provided evidence of tenofovir resistance in South African adults. The European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) issued clinical practice guidelines for HBV management in 2017. Huang et al. (2013) compared lamivudine plus adefovir with entecavir for lamivudine-resistant HBV. Lim et al. (2012) and Sherman et al. (2006) evaluated combination therapies for lamivudine-refractory HBV. Heo et al. (2012) and Byun et al. (2020) investigated switching to entecavir or TAF in drug-resistant HBV. Yamashige et al. (2021) assessed TAF effectiveness in patients with poor responses to prior therapies. Yang et al. (2020) reviewed antiviral regimens for entecavir-resistant HBV, while Liang et al. (2022) questioned the sufficiency of TDF monotherapy in treatment failures. Yim et al. (2020) studied tenofovir-based therapies for multidrug-resistant HBV. Chen et al. (2020) identified mutation patterns contributing to multidrug resistance. Wandera et al. (2022) reviewed HBV genetic multiplicity and resistance mutations in HBV/HIV co-infection. Alanine aminotransferase was deemed inadequate for detecting lamivudine resistance by LG et al. (2010). Terrault et al. (2016) provided AASLD guidelines for chronic HBV treatment. WHO guidelines addressed prevention, care, and treatment of chronic HBV, including mother-to-child transmission. Boeke et al. (2021) evaluated near point-of-care viral load implementation in sub-Saharan Africa.
